overview: This one-page file register inventories correspondence concerning U.S. assistance to the Kwantung Government with city planning and zoning in Dairen (modern Dalian). It records requests from Consul Grummon for American planning information and engineers’ maps, referrals to the Department of Commerce and Bureau of Standards, and the transmission of publications and other materials, including planning documents from Memphis and Nashville. The listed activity appears to have extended from at least September through July, with several actions explicitly associated with 1936.

subfiles.title: List of papers concerning city planning in Dairen
subfiles.about: A file register summarizes correspondence and transmitted publications relating to requests by the Kwantung Government for American assistance with planning and zoning Dairen.
subfiles.summary: The register lists requests from Consul Grummon for U.S. assistance, including planning information and engineers’ maps from American cities where zoning had been developed. It records referrals to the Department of Commerce and Bureau of Standards, followed by the forwarding of letters, documents, and publications. Frederic A. Delano of the National Resources Committee supplied a Memphis city plan and Nashville building-zone ordinance for transmission to Grummon.

interest: The register is useful for tracing an episode of transpacific technical exchange in urban planning under Japanese colonial administration. It shows Kwantung officials seeking concrete American models—not merely general advice—including engineers’ maps, zoning ordinances, and municipal plans. The references to Memphis and Nashville identify specific U.S. planning precedents that were selected for possible use in Dairen, while the register also reconstructs the bureaucratic path through the State Department, Commerce Department, Bureau of Standards, and National Resources Committee.
